entity_ranked_evidence.title: Our View: Breathtaking Generosity - Cape Cod Chronicle
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: by The Cape Cod Chronicle. Longtime readers know that we run two Helping Neighbors campaigns for the Family Pantry each year, one in the summer and one around the holidays. And during each campaign, going back as long as we can remember, there’ve been white-knuckle moments when we were certain we’d fall short of our fundraising target. But having raised only about $11,000 in the two weeks following the busy July 4 holiday, we figured we’d set too high a goal for the campaign. The funds donated by Cape Cod Chronicle readers are an essential part of the Family Pantry’s financial operations. We were pretty sure we were on track to fall short of our fundraising goal by Labor Day. We even put out an appeal in our Weekend Update Sunday warning that a surge of donations was needed. There were incredibly generous donations of $5,000 and $10,000, and on Monday, a man drove up to the Family Pantry office, handed the staff a check for $20,000, said thank you and walked away.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: Flood-hit Agriculture Needs Urgent Climate Action - daily-sun.com
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: Bangladesh’s agriculture is currently facing one of the most severe consequences of climate change. According to the latest data from the Ministry of Agriculture, floods have affected 43 districts across the country, damaging crops on 114,723 hectares of land. Of this, 107,845 hectares-- nearly 90 per cent of the total affected area-- are located in 16 districts. The worst-affected crops are Aus rice, Aman seedbeds and seasonal vegetables. Approximately 79,500 hectares of Aus rice, 10,504 hectares of Aman seedbeds, and 17,800 hectares of seasonal vegetables have been damaged. According to preliminary information from the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), Cumilla, crops on 19,899 hectares have been affected in Cumilla district alone. Of these, 19,477 hectares were standing crops, while crops on 2,671 hectares have already been damaged. A crop-wise assessment shows that transplanted Aman rice has suffered the largest overall impact, with 66 hectares damaged out of 16,200 hectares cultivated. A comprehensive recovery of agriculture, fisheries, and livestock is essential for restoring the rural economy.
